name: Invasive infections due to vancomycin-resistant enterococci

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: CDC/NHSN Criteria for Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcal Infection

criteria.description: Isolation of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus species from a normally sterile site (e.g., blood, cerebrospinal fluid, or deep tissue)
Presence of clinical signs consistent with invasive infection such as fever, hypotension, or localized signs of infection
Demonstration of vancomycin resistance by antimicrobial susceptibility testing
Imaging evidence of infection such as abscess or endocarditis
Exclusion of other causative pathogens by culture or molecular methods

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Isolation of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus from a sterile site with compatible clinical signs and confirmed antimicrobial resistance
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires both microbiological confirmation and clinical evidence of invasive infection.

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by repeated positive blood cultures
searchTerms: persistent bloodstream infection with resistant bacteria
heart valve infection with resistant bacteria

common.notes: Commonly in soft tissues or intra-abdominal sites

occasional.notes: If pulmonary involvement or septic emboli

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to septic emboli
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to septic emboli
brain symptoms from infected blood clots

laboratory: Positive blood cultures for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus species
Elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)
Antimicrobial susceptibility testing confirming vancomycin resistance
imaging: CT or MRI revealing abscess formation
Chest X-ray or CT showing septic emboli
genetic: Presence of vanA or vanB gene clusters conferring vancomycin resistance
other: Clinical signs of sepsis and localized infection
Histopathology of infected tissue showing enterococcal infiltration

distinguishingFeatures: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing shows vancomycin sensitivity
Similar clinical presentation but better response to vancomycin therapy
Isolation of Staphylococcus aureus or coagulase-negative staphylococci
Commonly associated with skin and soft tissue infections

redFlags: Persistent bacteremia despite appropriate antibiotic therapy
Evidence of endocarditis or metastatic abscess formation
references: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci (VRE) Infection. 2023.
López, A. et al. Clinical features and outcomes of invasive VRE infections. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2022.
Orphanet: Invasive infections due to vancomycin-resistant enterococci. ORPHA:90078.
